@graph.name: Do I need an SPS Commerce alternative to get restaurants ordering in an app?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. SPS Commerce goes on handling EDI for every partner that asks for it. What we add is aimed at the restaurants on your books that still get in touch by phone or by text: the chef names each item in our app, looks over the list and sends it.

@graph.name: Is VoiceOrder Solutions better than SPS Commerce?

acceptedAnswer.text: At one job: letting a restaurant without EDI software send you an order its chef has looked over, with no phone call. Everything EDI does for your chain customers, from ship notices to invoices, belongs to SPS Commerce, so we are not an SPS Commerce alternative.

@graph.name: Doesn't SPS Commerce already sell an ordering product?

acceptedAnswer.text: It has Order Central, built for stores ordering from their suppliers, with digital catalogs and an add-on for scanning and ordering straight from the aisle. Its page speaks to retailers. Ours is for a chef who prefers talking to browsing or scanning, ordering from the guide you prepared for that restaurant. SPS Commerce also sells PDF Order Automation, which moves PDF orders from accounts that do not use EDI into its EDI workflow. A chef's phone call leaves no PDF behind.

@graph.name: Are the two connected, and does my order desk keep typing orders?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Two separate companies make them, with no link between the two, and each one supports only its own software. Our EDI or API order bypasses SPS Commerce. If your ERP can take it that way, nobody retypes the order; the demo checks whether it can. Otherwise it arrives as an email attachment, and someone on your team enters it. That person skips taking the call, writing it out and repeating it back, since the chef confirmed every item in the app before sending. Whether SPS Commerce's PDF tool could read that attachment is a question to put to them: we have built nothing for it and promise nothing. Calls go on reaching your desk as they do today, and get no number from us. Your ERP holds customers, stock figures and invoices, as now; we keep the restaurant guides and their prices, plus whatever chefs have sent through the app.

@graph.name: Why not ask our restaurant accounts to send EDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: A large group with its own buying system might. Most small restaurants own nothing that could produce an EDI purchase order, while each new trading partner on SPS Commerce is set up and tested before it goes live. The app asks a restaurant for a phone and a few minutes of the chef's time.

@graph.name: Do app orders come with the paperwork an EDI order gets?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. We deliver the order, with an order number and a timestamp, and the restaurant gets a confirmation in the app. Acknowledgments, shipping paperwork and bills come from your own systems, and for EDI accounts from SPS Commerce. The app can still pass on a wrong item if the chef misses it, but the chef reads the list on screen before it goes, rather than hearing it read back over a call.

@graph.name: How soon can we begin, and what does it cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most distributors can start in 24 to 48 hours, and nothing in SPS Commerce changes. You share each account's usual items, usually as a spreadsheet export, and we load them into our admin and set up each account. The restaurants install our app, and most send in their first order that same day. SPS Commerce publishes its fees for adding trading partners and users; we quote per distributor. An SPS Commerce replacement means moving all your trading partners to another provider, whereas we leave those connections alone.

@graph.name: Where do the SPS Commerce details on this page come from?

acceptedAnswer.text: We read spscommerce.com on 9 November 2026: the homepage, the Fulfillment, Order Central, MAX, Distribution and Grocery & Food pages, What is EDI, the page defining Fulfillment fees, and its article on automating PDF orders. Facts about the other ordering software came from searching the web that day. If SPS Commerce has changed anything since, tell us so we can fix our copy.
